hints.content: Let's consider each object and see if we can get a rectangle cross-section by slicing it perpendicular to its base/face.

Here are all the cross-sections we can get by slicing the cone perpendicular to its base:



[[☃ image 1]]

The cross-section is never a rectangle.

options.alt: A cone with a plane perpendicular to the cone's base passing through it and showing every cross-section as it passes through.

hints.content:
Here are all the cross-sections we can get by slicing the pyramid perpendicular to its base:



[[☃ image 1]]

The cross-section is never a rectangle.

options.alt: A rectangular pyramid with a plane perpendicular to the pyramid's base passing through it and showing every cross-section as it horizontally passes through.

hints.content:
Here are all the cross-sections we can get by slicing the cylinder perpendicular to its base:



[[☃ image 1]]

No matter where we slice the cylinder, the shape is always a rectangle.

options.alt: A cylinder with a plane perpendicular to the cylinder's base passing through it and showing every cross-section as it horizontally passes through.

hints.content:
Here are all the cross-sections we can get by slicing the sphere:



[[☃ image 1]]

The cross-section is always a circle.

options.alt: A sphere with a plane passing through it and showing every cross-section as it vertically passes through.
